intro: The certifications you're working toward, in the order that makes sense. Mark each one Planned, Studying, Exam booked or Passed. Cards for the ones you're studying go into your daily review.

certs.name: LEED Green Associate (v5)
certs.tagline: The entry credential for green building, now tested on LEED v5.
certs.fit: Shows Arup, Gensler, Arcadis and SF Environment you speak LEED. It's the baseline for sustainability roles in buildings, and the first step to LEED AP BD+C.

facts.v: Final v5 exam (beta ran April 28 to June 30, 2026). Third-party guides report 100 multiple-choice questions, 2 hours, 170 of 200 to pass; confirm in the candidate handbook.
No experience required.
LEED Core Concepts Guide (5th ed.), Foundations of LEED, Guide to Certification: Commercial, LEED Rating System Selection Guidance
Continuing education every 2 years (15 hours for Green Associates).
LEED AP BD+C. The v5 AP exam's final version is expected February 2027.

plan: Week 1: LEED v5 basics in this pack, then Chapter 1 (LEED Process) of the study guide
Week 2: the v5 scorecard: learn the 16 prerequisites and the points per category
Week 3: Energy and Atmosphere and Materials and Resources (most points, most v5 changes)
Week 4: the other categories, then a full practice exam
Week 5: review missed questions, then book the exam on usgbc.org
certs.check: Canopy's 9-chapter study guide follows the classic Green Associate book order and was written for v4. Learn the v5 names, prerequisites and points from this pack: that's where the exam changed most.

items: Operational Carbon Projection and Decarbonization Plan

cards.q: Which version of LEED is the Green Associate exam based on now?
cards.explain: The LEED v4 Green Associate exam was last offered April 26, 2026. The exam is now based entirely on LEED v5.

cards.q: What are LEED v5's three impact areas?
cards.a: Decarbonization, quality of life, ecological conservation and restoration
cards.explain: Every LEED v5 credit maps to one or more of these impact areas.

cards.q: How many total points are possible in LEED v5 BD+C: New Construction?
cards.explain: Same total as v4: 110 possible points.

cards.q: How many points does a LEED v5 project need for Certified?
cards.explain: Certified 40-49, Silver 50-59, Gold 60-79, Platinum 80+.

cards.q: How many points does a LEED v5 project need for Gold?
cards.explain: Certified 40-49, Silver 50-59, Gold 60-79, Platinum 80+.

cards.q: Besides 80+ points, what else does a LEED v5 BD+C New Construction Platinum project need?
cards.a: Required minimums in Electrification, Energy Efficiency, Renewables and Embodied Carbon
cards.explain: Appendix I: 5 Electrification points, 8 Enhanced Energy Efficiency points, 100% renewable energy for site energy use, and a 20% embodied carbon reduction.
wrong: A LEED Fellow on the team

cards.q: For LEED v5 NC Platinum, how much embodied carbon reduction is required?
cards.explain: MRc2 Reduce Embodied Carbon: a 20% reduction is required for Platinum projects.

cards.q: For LEED v5 NC Platinum, how much of site energy use must come from renewables?
cards.explain: EAc4 Renewable Energy: 100% of site energy use from any combination of Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 renewable energy.

cards.q: How many prerequisites does LEED v5 BD+C: New Construction have?
cards.explain: 3 IP + 1 SS + 2 WE + 5 EA + 2 MR + 3 EQ = 16 (Core and Shell adds Tenant Guidelines).

cards.q: Which credit category is worth the most points in LEED v5 NC?
cards.explain: EA is 33 of 110 points. Next: MR 18, LT 15, EQ 13.

cards.q: What is LEED v5's first credit category called?
cards.explain: It holds the three assessment prerequisites plus the Integrative Design Process credit.

cards.q: Name the three IP prerequisites in LEED v5.
cards.a: Climate Resilience, Human Impact, and Carbon Assessments
cards.explain: IPp1 Climate Resilience Assessment, IPp2 Human Impact Assessment, IPp3 Carbon Assessment.

cards.q: What does the Climate Resilience Assessment prerequisite cover?
cards.a: Observed, projected and future natural hazards for the project
cards.explain: Its intent: assess natural hazards to raise awareness, increase transparency of risks and reduce vulnerabilities.

cards.q: What does the Human Impact Assessment prerequisite look at?
cards.a: The social context of the community, workforce and supply chain
cards.explain: Intent: guide development by understanding the local social context and addressing potential social inequities.

cards.q: What does the Carbon Assessment prerequisite cover?
cards.a: Long-term carbon: on-site combustion, grid electricity, refrigerants and embodied carbon
cards.explain: IPp3 aims to understand and reduce long-term direct and indirect carbon emissions.

cards.q: Which EA prerequisite asks teams to project long-term operational carbon?
cards.a: Operational Carbon Projection and Decarbonization Plan
cards.explain: EAp1 helps stakeholders see how today's design decisions affect long-term operational emissions.

cards.q: List LEED v5's five EA prerequisites.
cards.a: Carbon projection plan, minimum efficiency, fundamental commissioning, metering, refrigerant management
cards.explain: EAp1 Operational Carbon Projection and Decarbonization Plan, EAp2 Minimum Energy Efficiency, EAp3 Fundamental Commissioning, EAp4 Energy Metering and Reporting, EAp5 Fundamental Refrigerant Management.

cards.q: What is the intent of the Electrification credit (EAc1)?
cards.a: Design buildings that don't burn fuel on site
cards.explain: Better indoor and outdoor air quality and low-carbon operations as the grid gets cleaner.

cards.q: Which new v5 EA credit rewards managing building loads in response to grid conditions?
cards.explain: It positions buildings as active partners in grid decarbonization, reliability and affordability.

cards.q: What does Reduce Peak Thermal Loads (EAc2) aim to do?
cards.a: Minimize demand on grid resources and improve resilience
cards.explain: Worth up to 5 points in NC.

cards.q: Which two MR prerequisites are new in LEED v5?
cards.a: Planning for Zero Waste Operations and Quantify and Assess Embodied Carbon
cards.explain: MRp1 and MRp2. Every project now quantifies embodied carbon of its structure, enclosure and hardscape.
wrong: Storage and Collection of Recyclables and PBT Source Reduction
Construction Waste Plan and Low-Emitting Materials

cards.q: What does MRp2 Quantify and Assess Embodied Carbon cover?
cards.a: Embodied carbon of the structure, enclosure and hardscape
cards.explain: It quantifies those impacts and identifies the top sources of embodied carbon.

cards.q: Which LEED v5 credit replaced Innovation and Regional Priority?
cards.explain: PRc1 Project Priorities (up to 9 points) plus PRc2 LEED AP (1 point) = 10 points.

cards.q: How many points is the LEED AP credit worth in v5?
cards.explain: PRc2 LEED AP rewards having a LEED AP on the team.

cards.q: Which LT credit is worth the most in LEED v5 NC?
cards.explain: It rewards building where infrastructure exists, walkability and less driving.

cards.q: Which v5 SS prerequisite limits construction disturbance and protects native vegetation and soils?
cards.explain: SSp1 is Sustainable Sites' only prerequisite.

cards.q: Name the two Water Efficiency prerequisites in LEED v5.
cards.a: Water Metering and Reporting, Minimum Water Efficiency
cards.explain: WEp1 and WEp2. Enhanced Water Efficiency (WEc2) is worth up to 8 points.
wrong: Outdoor and Indoor Water Use Reduction

cards.q: Name the three EQ prerequisites in LEED v5 NC.
cards.a: Construction Management, Fundamental Air Quality, No Smoking or Vehicle Idling
cards.explain: EQp1-3. Occupant Experience (EQc2) is the largest EQ credit at 7 points.

cards.q: Which EQ credit supports diverse occupant needs and a sense of belonging?
cards.explain: One of the quality-of-life credits new in v5.

cards.q: About what share of LEED v5 points goes to decarbonization?
cards.explain: USGBC weights decarbonization about 50%, quality of life about 25% and ecological conservation and restoration about 25%.

cards.q: What are the four LEED v5 rating systems?
cards.a: BD+C, ID+C, O+M and LEED for Cities
cards.explain: BD+C for new construction and major renovation, ID+C for interiors, O+M for existing buildings. LEED for Cities was still a draft in October 2026.

cards.q: Which references does USGBC list for the v5 Green Associate exam?
cards.a: LEED Core Concepts Guide (5th ed.), Foundations of LEED, Guide to Certification: Commercial, Rating System Selection Guidance
cards.explain: Listed on USGBC's LEED v5 exam information page.

cards.q: Can you sit for the LEED AP with Specialty v5 exam if you earned your Green Associate on v4?
cards.explain: USGBC: Green Associate holders, regardless of exam version, are eligible for the AP with Specialty v5 exam.
wrong: No, you must retake GA on v5

certs.name: TRUE Advisor (zero waste)
certs.tagline: A short online course and exam on zero waste and the TRUE certification.
certs.fit: A fast win. Zero waste is a core SF Environment program, and every LEED v5 project now needs a Planning for Zero Waste Operations prerequisite.

facts.v: 12 narrated online modules, then a 75-question end-of-course exam
None
$450, or $350 for USGBC members (access for 180 days)
Finish the course and pass the exam within 180 days of registering
7.5 continuing-education hours, which count toward your LEED credential
USGBC launched TRUE v2 in October 2026; check which version the course covers when you register.

plan: Learn the flashcards in this pack (1 week)
Register and work through the 12 modules (about 2 weeks)
Take the 75-question exam before your 180 days run out
certs.check: Course topics and price are from the GBCI page in October 2026.

cards.q: What does TRUE certify?
cards.explain: TRUE (Total Resource Use and Efficiency) is GBCI's zero waste certification.

cards.q: What does TRUE stand for?
cards.explain: TRUE is administered by GBCI, the same body that runs LEED credentials.
wrong: Transparent Reporting of Use and Emissions

cards.q: What minimum diversion rate does a TRUE project need?
cards.explain: TRUE v2 keeps the 90% diversion requirement.

cards.q: Does waste-to-energy or incineration count as diversion under TRUE?
cards.explain: Approved strategies include reduction, reuse, composting, recycling and anaerobic digestion.

cards.q: Are there eligibility requirements for the TRUE Advisor credential?
cards.explain: Anyone can register, take the course and the exam.

cards.q: How many questions are on the TRUE Advisor exam?
cards.explain: The exam comes at the end of the online course.

cards.q: How long do you have to finish the TRUE Advisor course and exam?
cards.explain: The fee covers 180 days of access.

cards.q: How many online modules does the TRUE Advisor course have?
cards.explain: Narrated modules plus downloadable resources and guided notes.

cards.q: How many CE hours does passing TRUE Advisor earn?
cards.explain: Useful toward LEED credential maintenance.

cards.q: Which TRUE topics come before recycling and composting?
cards.explain: Zero waste works from the top of the hierarchy down: design waste out first.

cards.q: What is a zero waste audit for?
cards.a: Measuring what's in the waste stream to find diversion opportunities
cards.explain: Audits give the baseline numbers TRUE reporting relies on.

cards.q: Which LEED v5 prerequisite connects directly to TRUE?
cards.a: MRp1 Planning for Zero Waste Operations
cards.explain: Every LEED v5 BD+C project must plan for zero waste operations.

cards.q: What is 'bin right-sizing'?
cards.a: Matching container size and pickup frequency to actual waste volumes
cards.explain: Right-sizing cuts hauling costs and emissions.

cards.q: Which TRUE topic covers making sure purchased goods create less waste?
cards.explain: Purchasing upstream is one of TRUE's credit areas.

cards.q: What does 'closed loop' mean in zero waste?
cards.a: Materials go back into making new products, often for the same user
cards.explain: Example: buying recycled paper made from your own office's recycled paper.

certs.name: WELL Accredited Professional
certs.tagline: The health and well-being credential for buildings and workplaces.
certs.fit: The Arup posting accepts WELL AP. It's especially valuable at Gensler, which designs a lot of workplaces where WELL is common.

facts.v: WELL v2: 10 concepts plus Innovation
Third-party guides report 115 multiple-choice questions in 2.5 hours, scored 125 to 200 with 170 to pass. Confirm in IWBI's candidate handbook.
Third-party guides list about $299, with a lower student price. Check IWBI's current fee.
No formal prerequisites; WELL knowledge recommended
Continuing education every 2 years

plan: Learn the 10 concepts and the certification levels in this pack
Read the WELL v2 standard online, one concept a day
Take practice questions, then register through IWBI
certs.check: Exam length, scoring and fees here come from third-party guides; IWBI's candidate handbook is the official source.

cards.q: Who runs the WELL Building Standard?
cards.explain: WELL focuses on human health and well-being in buildings.

cards.q: How many concepts does WELL v2 have?
cards.explain: Air, Water, Nourishment, Light, Movement, Thermal Comfort, Sound, Materials, Mind, Community.

cards.q: Name the 10 WELL v2 concepts.
cards.a: Air, Water, Nourishment, Light, Movement, Thermal Comfort, Sound, Materials, Mind, Community
cards.explain: Innovation is an extra category on top of the 10.
wrong: Energy, Water, Waste, Sites, Air, Light, Sound, Comfort, Mind, Equity
Air, Water, Food, Fitness, Comfort, Mind, Sleep, Light, Noise, Safety
Site, Water, Energy, Materials, Air, Light, Sound, Thermal, Mind, Community

cards.q: What are the WELL v2 certification levels?
cards.explain: Bronze 40, Silver 50, Gold 60, Platinum 80 points.

cards.q: How many points for WELL Gold?
cards.explain: Bronze 40, Silver 50, Gold 60, Platinum 80.

cards.q: In WELL, what is a precondition?
cards.a: A required feature every project must meet
cards.explain: Optimizations are the optional features that earn points.

cards.q: In WELL, what is an optimization?
cards.a: An optional feature that earns points
cards.explain: Preconditions are mandatory; optimizations are chosen to reach a level.

cards.q: What makes WELL different from LEED in how it's verified?
cards.a: On-site performance verification testing (air, water, light, sound)
cards.explain: WELL checks how the building actually performs for people.

cards.q: How often does WELL certification need renewal?
cards.explain: WELL certification is renewed with new performance data.

cards.q: Which WELL concept covers mental health, stress and restorative spaces?
cards.explain: Mind features support cognitive and emotional health.

cards.q: Which WELL concept covers circadian lighting and glare?
cards.explain: Light features cover visual comfort and circadian health.

cards.q: Which WELL concept covers active design, stairs and ergonomics?
cards.explain: Movement encourages physical activity throughout the day.

cards.q: Which WELL concept covers healthy food, fruit and vegetables, and mindful eating?
cards.explain: Nourishment covers food availability, labeling and eating spaces.

cards.q: Which WELL concept covers health benefits, inclusive design and emergency preparedness?
cards.explain: Community addresses policies and the social environment.

cards.q: Which WELL concept limits hazardous ingredients such as lead and asbestos?
cards.explain: Materials reduces exposure to hazardous building materials.

cards.q: Is there a formal experience requirement to take the WELL AP exam?
cards.explain: WELL project experience is recommended but not required.

cards.q: Which health credential did the Arup graduate posting accept along with LEED AP?
cards.explain: The Arup posting also named Fitwel and Envision.

certs.name: Envision Sustainability Professional
certs.tagline: Sustainability for infrastructure: roads, water, energy, parks and transit.
certs.fit: Arup, Arcadis and AECOM are infrastructure firms, and Envision is named in the Arup posting. It's also used on public works, so it's useful for city jobs.

facts.v: Training course (online or live), then an online exam
75 multiple-choice questions; 75% to pass (ISI packet)
Usually $450 to $800 including the exam, depending on the provider (APWA, ASCE, ISI). Some public agencies get a $250 rate.
Envision v3: 64 credits in 5 categories
None

plan: Learn the 5 categories and achievement levels in this pack
Take an ISI-approved training course (often 4 sessions of 2 hours)
Pass the 75-question exam
certs.check: Prices vary by provider and year; check the course page before you register.

cards.q: What does Envision rate?
cards.explain: Roads, bridges, water systems, energy, parks, transit and more.

cards.q: Who runs Envision?
cards.explain: ISI was founded by ASCE, APWA and ACEC.

cards.q: How many credits are in Envision v3?
cards.explain: Spread across 5 categories.

cards.q: Name Envision's 5 categories.
cards.a: Quality of Life, Leadership, Resource Allocation, Natural World, Climate and Resilience
cards.explain: QL 14, LD 12, RA 14, NW 14, CR 10 credits.

cards.q: Which Envision category covers wellbeing, mobility and community?
cards.explain: 14 credits.

cards.q: Which Envision category covers collaboration, planning and economy?
cards.explain: 12 credits.

cards.q: Which Envision category covers materials, energy and water?
cards.explain: 14 credits.

cards.q: Which Envision category covers siting, conservation and ecology?
cards.explain: 14 credits.

cards.q: Which Envision category covers emissions and resilience?
cards.explain: 10 credits.

cards.q: What are Envision's levels of achievement, lowest to highest?
cards.explain: Each credit is scored by how far it goes, up to restoring natural or social systems.

cards.q: What are Envision's project award levels?
cards.explain: Awards are based on the share of applicable points a project earns.

cards.q: How many questions are on the ENV SP exam?
cards.explain: 75% is needed to pass, per ISI.

cards.q: What score do you need to pass the ENV SP exam?
cards.explain: From ISI's ENV SP packet.

cards.q: Why is Envision useful for a career at Arup or Arcadis?
cards.a: They're major infrastructure firms and Envision rates infrastructure
cards.explain: The Arup graduate posting named Envision directly.

certs.name: SEED (Social Economic Environmental Design)
certs.tagline: Public interest design: projects certified for their social, economic and environmental outcomes.
certs.fit: Ties design to community outcomes, which is the heart of SF Environment's engagement work and Gensler's community-focused projects.

facts.v: Design projects, not people. A panel of SEED Certified professionals reviews each project.
The SEED Evaluator, a free online tool that is also the application form
3 phases, each reviewed by the panel
Free to register; processing fees on a sliding scale (professional, nonprofit, student)
Public Interest Design Institute courses have taught the SEED process. Check seednetwork.org for current sessions.

plan: Learn how SEED works with this pack
Register for the free SEED Evaluator and walk through a past project of yours
Ask the SEED Network about current Public Interest Design training
certs.check: SEED certifies projects; there is no individual exam like LEED. If you meant a different SEED credential, tell Claude and this pack will be swapped.

cards.q: What does SEED stand for?
cards.explain: SEED looks at a project's social, economic and environmental outcomes together.

cards.q: What does SEED certify: people or projects?
cards.explain: SEED Certification is granted to design projects after independent review.

cards.q: Who reviews SEED certification applications?
cards.a: A panel of SEED Certified professionals
cards.explain: Independent third-party review at each phase.

cards.q: What is the SEED Evaluator?
cards.a: A free online tool that guides and documents a project; also the application form
cards.explain: It helps assess community challenges, set goals and document outcomes.

cards.q: How many phases does SEED Certification have?
cards.explain: Each phase is reviewed by the panel.

cards.q: How are SEED processing fees set?
cards.a: On a sliding scale by project type
cards.explain: Professional, nonprofit and student projects pay different fees.

cards.q: What kind of design is SEED part of?
cards.explain: Design that serves communities, often with people who have limited voice in public decisions.

cards.q: What is a core SEED practice when working with a community?
cards.a: Inclusive, participatory decision-making with community members
cards.explain: Projects are guided by the community's own goals.

certs.name: Certified Industrial Hygienist
certs.issuer: Board for Global EHS Credentialing (BGC, formerly ABIH)
certs.tagline: The top credential for protecting workers and occupants from health hazards.
certs.fit: A long-term goal for environmental health and safety (EHS) and indoor air quality work. It connects with WELL and LEED indoor air credits.

facts.v: 180 multiple-choice questions (150 scored, 30 pilot), about 5 hours
Strict: a degree, industrial hygiene coursework, ethics training, and documented years of professional IH experience with references. Check BGC's current tables.
Realistic only after a few years working in industrial hygiene or EHS
16 subject areas, including air sampling, toxicology, biostatistics and epidemiology, and ventilation
BGC Certification Maintenance Process and Code of Ethics

plan: Learn the IH basics in this pack now (they also help with WELL and LEED indoor air)
Look for EHS or industrial hygiene roles or graduate IH coursework
Check BGC's eligibility tables once you have qualifying experience
certs.check: Eligibility details (degree, academic hours, years of experience) change; confirm on gobgc.org before planning around them.

cards.q: What does a CIH do?
cards.a: Anticipates, recognizes, evaluates and controls workplace health hazards
cards.explain: Industrial hygiene protects workers and building occupants.

cards.q: Who grants the CIH?
cards.a: BGC, the Board for Global EHS Credentialing (formerly ABIH)
cards.explain: The American Board of Industrial Hygiene renamed itself BGC.

cards.q: How many questions are on the CIH exam?
cards.explain: About 5 hours, with an optional break.

cards.q: List the hierarchy of controls, most to least effective.
cards.explain: PPE is the last line of defense.

cards.q: What is an OSHA PEL?
cards.a: A legally enforceable permissible exposure limit
cards.explain: PELs are OSHA regulations; many are decades old.

cards.q: What is an ACGIH TLV?
cards.a: A health-based guideline (threshold limit value), not a law
cards.explain: TLVs are often stricter than OSHA PELs.

cards.q: What does NIOSH publish?
cards.explain: NIOSH is the research agency; OSHA enforces.

cards.q: What is a TWA?
cards.a: A time-weighted average exposure, usually over 8 hours
cards.explain: Most exposure limits are written as 8-hour TWAs.

cards.q: What is a STEL?
cards.a: A short-term exposure limit, usually 15 minutes
cards.explain: It limits brief peaks above the TWA.
wrong: A ceiling that can never be crossed

cards.q: What is a ceiling limit?
cards.a: A concentration that should never be exceeded at any time
cards.explain: Different from a STEL, which is an average over 15 minutes.

cards.q: What are the main routes of entry for hazardous substances?
cards.explain: Inhalation is the most common route at work.

cards.q: What is OSHA's noise PEL?
cards.a: 90 dBA as an 8-hour TWA (5 dB exchange rate)
cards.explain: The action level for hearing conservation is 85 dBA.

cards.q: What is NIOSH's recommended noise limit?
cards.a: 85 dBA as an 8-hour TWA (3 dB exchange rate)
cards.explain: Stricter than OSHA's 90 dBA PEL.

cards.q: What is local exhaust ventilation?
cards.a: Capturing contaminants at the source before they spread
cards.explain: Example: a fume hood or welding extractor. More effective than general dilution.

cards.q: What does indoor CO2 usually indicate in buildings?
cards.a: How well the space is ventilated for the number of people
cards.explain: High CO2 suggests too little outdoor air for occupancy.

cards.q: Which building hazards often involve an industrial hygienist?
cards.explain: Common in renovation, indoor air quality and green building projects.
